title: First impressions of New Orleans and Kid Rene playing 'Panama'
summary: In New Orleans Moore played with Kid Rene, and he stresses the lazy tempo of local bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: It was a good experience for me to go to New Orleans because I hear so much about jazz in New Orleans. I met all the important people there that are wailing in New Orleans.
Well, everyone there, of course, knew Louis Armstrong and he was certainly someone who meant a lot to you, I'm sure, and was going to mean a lot to you.

Yes, I know you know most of the people in New Orleans, but I will start out with people that I have worked with -- Sidney Bechet, Louis Armstrong, Albert Nicholas, Paul Barbarin -- while I was in New Orleans I happened to play with a guy called Kid Rene' who in history books is one of the greats, and it was wonderful to hear him blow "Panama." When they blow "Panama" in New Orleans, they didn't play fast, they played it at a smooth tempo and every note that Kid Rene' played meant something, the phrasing, the

chord construction, he would go up and down, it was wonderful. I always asked him, during that one night I was with him, "Please play Panamá again."

Well, you found this music in New Orleans at that time very different from the kind of music you played in California, I mean as far as just how the musicians were improvising, it was more of a collective improvising as opposed to perhaps an orchestral and blues type of playing?

Yes, even today as it was in the days when I was in New Orleans, I don't know why, but the fastest they want to play and the loudest they want to play, they always invariably think they're making a big impression by playing fast and playing loud, but it wasn't like that with the bands I was with in New Orleans. They played that lazy kind of rhythm and that's why I appreciated Kid Rene' and some of the band around this and Celestin went the same way.
